name: TimeTac
description: TimeTac time and attendance for DACH teams: time trackings, users, projects, tasks, absences, departments and the live attendance overview. REST API v4 at api.timetac.com, OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
instructions:
**Your account name is part of every URL.** TimeTac's API lives at `https://api.timetac.com/<account>/v4/<resource>/<action>/`. Set `TIMETAC_ACCOUNT` to your company account name (the name you log in with); the adapter builds the URL from it.

**Getting API credentials**
1. API access is not open by default: contact TimeTac support (support@timetac.com) to have it enabled for your account.
2. In TimeTac open your account settings → **API Credentials** and create a client. You receive a **client id** and a **client secret**.
3. Set `TIMETAC_ACCOUNT`, `TIMETAC_CLIENT_ID` and `TIMETAC_CLIENT_SECRET`. The adapter uses the OAuth 2.0 *client credentials* grant against `https://api.timetac.com/<account>/auth/oauth2/token` and fetches a new access token on its own whenever the old one expires. No browser authorization step is needed.

**Reads end in `/read/`.** TimeTac's API is not REST-shaped: the list endpoint for a resource is `<resource>/read/`. Filters are plain query parameters named after the resource's fields, with an optional operator: `active=1`, `department_id=3`, or `_op__start_time=gteq&start_time=2026-09-01 00:00:00`. Operators are `eq` (default), `gt`, `gteq`, `lt`, `lteq`, `in` (pipe-separated list, e.g. `_op__id=in&id=1|2|3`), `betw` (pipe-separated range) and `like`. The tools' `filter` argument takes that query-string fragment verbatim.

**Paging and sorting** use `_limit` (default 100), `_offset`, `_order_by` (a field name) and `_sort_direction` (`ASC` or `DESC`); the tools expose them as `limit`, `offset`, `order_by` and `sort_direction`.

**Responses are wrapped** in `{"Success": true, "NumResults": n, "Results": [...]}`. An empty `Results` with `Success: true` means the filter matched nothing, not that the call failed; on an error `Success` is false and `Error` / `ErrorMessage` explain why.

**Not run against a live account.** The URL, token endpoint and parameters follow TimeTac's API documentation (docs.timetac.com) and its v4 OpenAPI file; the per-resource field names come from that documentation too. Check the docs before concluding a credential is wrong.

**Cloud reachability**: `api.timetac.com` is public with a valid certificate.

tools.name: timetac_list_users
tools.description: List the users in the TimeTac account with their name, personnel number, department and active state. The quickest check that the OAuth client works.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `active=1&department_id=3`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_list_time_trackings
tools.description: Read time trackings in a date range: start, end, duration, the user and the task booked against. This is the core reporting query.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `_op__start_time=betw&start_time=2026-09-01 00:00:00|2026-09-30 23:59:59&user_id=5`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_list_projects
tools.description: List projects with their client, target duration and done state, so a time tracking can be attributed to a piece of work.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `is_done=0&client_id=4`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_list_tasks
tools.description: List tasks — the things users actually clock onto — with the project they belong to (mother_id) and whether they are done.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `mother_id=12&is_done=0`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_list_absences
tools.description: List absences (holiday, sick leave, special leave) with their type, date range and approval state, for the roster view.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `user_id=5&_op__from_date=gteq&from_date=2026-09-01`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_list_departments
tools.description: List the departments configured in the account, so users and reports can be grouped the way the org chart does.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `active=1`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.

tools.name: timetac_get_live_status
tools.description: Read the live attendance overview (userStatusOverview): per user whether a time tracking is running, on which task and project, and current absences. Answers 'who is working right now'.

filter.description: Query-string filter on the resource's fields, passed verbatim, e.g. `department_id=3&is_running=1`. Operators via _op__<field>: eq, gt, gteq, lt, lteq, in (pipe list), betw (pipe range), like.
